## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Jìngfàn wáng bān nièpán jīng* (T512) is a one-fascicle short sūtra translated by the Liú-Sòng monk [沮渠京聲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%AE%E6%B8%A0%E4%BA%AC%E8%81%B2) Jǔqú Jīngshēng. *Jìngfàn wáng* 淨飯王 is the Chinese semantic translation of King Śuddhodana, the Buddha's father. The sūtra narrates the death of Śuddhodana and the Buddha's filial response — washing the body, leading the funeral procession, and giving the eulogistic discourse.

**Abstract**

The Śuddhodana parinirvāṇa narrative is foundational for Buddhist conceptions of filial piety, often invoked in Chinese Confucian-Buddhist debates as evidence that the Buddha himself honored his father. Jǔqú Jīngshēng was a member of the Northern Liáng royal house (the Jǔqú clan) who fled to Liú-Sòng territory after the fall of his dynasty in 439 CE; he became a translator at Jiànkāng. His translation activity is dated 455–464 CE.
